speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the location and severity of your flank pain, and has it been constant or intermittent? Also, are you experiencing any changes in your urine, such as color, smell, or frequency?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling tired, feverish, and I have flank pain. These symptoms continued even after my sinus symptoms improved.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see that the pain and fever persist despite your sinus infection clearing up; could you tell me if you are experiencing any pain or burning when you urinate, or if your urine looks cloudy or bloody? Do you also have any nausea, vomiting, or chills accompanying these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: I was first treated with amoxicillin for sinusitis and developed a rash. Then the antibiotic was changed to cephalexin for another week, and the rash went away.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the rash that appeared after taking amoxicillin, I need to ask if you are currently experiencing any shortness of breath, swelling in your face or limbs, or if you have noticed any new skin lesions. Also, has your urine output decreased significantly, or do you feel any pain when passing it?

speaker: Patient
text: I do not have nausea, vomiting, or burning with urination. I also have not noticed a major change in urine color.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a history of kidney stones or any known kidney issues, and has your fever been measured to be above 101°F? Given your symptoms and antibiotic history, I would like to check your kidney function and urine for infection. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, REQUEST TEST: Creatinine, REQUEST TEST: CBC.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Temperature: 37.9°C (100.2°F); Blood Pressure: 145/90 mmHg; Heart Rate: 75 bpm; Respiratory Rate: 16 breaths/min. Abdomen: Mild flank tenderness; Renal Angles: Mild tenderness on percussion. Serum Biochemistry: Urea Elevated, Creatinine Elevated. Urinalysis: Leukocyturia Present, Bacterial Culture Negative, Cytospin (Hansel’s Solution) shows 3% binucleated cells with eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm. Note: CBC results are not available in the provided data.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The urinalysis showing binucleated cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm, combined with your fever, elevated creatinine, and recent antibiotic exposure, strongly suggests an allergic reaction in the kidneys. Do you have any history of atopic conditions like asthma, eczema, or hay fever, and did you experience any itching or hives alongside your initial rash?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Interstitial Nephritis
